newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise on Brazil issue talk.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise on Brazil issue talk.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose Wednesday on the back of talk of a Brazilian bond issue and firm U.S. Treasuries.

"The market was very firm early on talk of a Brazil issue but it has come off slightly," said a trader, noting that this could be the first sign of profit-taking to come after the surge in prices since Friday.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.30 to 119.90, and Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/2 to 85-1/8.
Local fund managers have been busy buyers in the last two sessions, but with the market having risen sharply in three days in a row, profit-taking could set in.
"I think the market is ready for a correction, particularly since its risen mainly on overseas influences," said another trader at a large foreign bank.

Still, Argentina's bonds were kept afloat Wednesday by an expected launch of a $750 million global offering by Brazil and more talk of the possibility of an upgrade of Brazilian debt by the credit rating agencies.
No specific news was expected through the session on the domestic front, but statements on the government's labor market reforms continue to be watched closely.
